correctness.rationale: The OLS intercept identity decomposes into independent Gaussian sample-mean and residual terms. Wick formulas, a chi-square radius, and spherical-moment ratios give an exact rational risk for every integer \(n\ge2\). The difference from \(6/n\) reduces to the sign of a quartic polynomial, negative at \(n=2,3\) and positive from \(n=4\); 1,790 exact-rational assertions and independent simulation diagnostics agree. No finite numerical check is treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The cubic residual is the first nontrivial odd Gaussian Hermite component after removing the linear control, making its exact finite-sample OLS risk a natural benchmark rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. A complete all-n risk classification reveals that fitting a control from the same data can outperform even the population-best fixed coefficient for all n>=4, despite initial variance inflation at \(n=2,3\). This distinguishes practical finite-budget performance from asymptotic oracle statements without claiming broad algorithm dominance.
